title: 12th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with the minutes of earlier sittings being accepted, Hijri New Year greetings from the Speaker and announcements of committee membership changes. The opposition MDP's urgent motion on unpaid government money for students abroad was put to a vote on whether to debate it and did not get enough votes (12 for, 59 against). The Majlis then began the preliminary debate on the government-backed bill to amend the Copyright and Related Rights Act (Law 23/2010), sponsored by Fathimath Sauda; most speakers backed it, while several exchanges and points of order were about the urgent motion and the MDP. A 30-minute break was taken and the bill debate was still going at the end of this part. This part covers the preliminary debate on the government-sponsored bill to amend the Copyright and Related Rights Act (Act 23/2010), tabled by the Nilandhoo member Fathimath Sauda. Members who spoke backed the bill as protecting artists, writers and small businesses, with several urging that it go to committee and that enforcement of the law be strengthened. Much of the debate also turned to the MDP's urgent question that morning on overseas students' allowances: ruling-party members called it a delaying tactic and criticised MDP absences from the floor, while MDP members raised points of order and said the students' problem was real. A recess ran from 12:34 to 13:06; the sitting was then closed with no vote on the bill, because nobody else was present to take the floor, and the next sitting was set for 9 July 2024. The text includes a recorded vote (12 yes, 59 no) on whether to debate the urgent question.

items.title: Opening of the sitting and prayers
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 57 present, 2 on leave, none on official travel

items.title: Approval of minutes of sittings 5 to 8 (2024/5 to 2024/8)
items.outcome: accepted as no amendments were submitted

items.title: Urgent matter by Ibrahim Nazil (South Hithadhoo) on government payments owed to students studying abroad on scholarship or loan
items.outcome: motion to debate did not pass 12-59 (36 needed)

items.title: Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Copyright and Related Rights Act (Law 23/2010)
items.outcome: debated; still ongoing at end of this part

items.title: Preliminary debate on the Bill to amend the Copyright and Related Rights Act (Act 23/2010), sponsored for the government by Fathimath Sauda (Nilandhoo)
items.outcome: debated; no vote taken before the sitting closed

items.title: Closing of the sitting

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Moved the urgent matter: the government has not paid money owed to students abroad, risking evictions, blacklisting and hardship.
In the bill debate, said all matters raised in the Majlis concern citizens' rights, including student fees and stipends.
Raised a point of order saying there are students who hold evidence that they were not paid; the Chair declined it.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill and thanked the sponsor, saying the amendments protect creators.
Rejected the MDP urgent question and said the government had already paid overseas students.
Said the MDP members who asked to speak were not on the floor.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised two points of order that members should not disrupt a speaker.
Supported the bill and cited a Maldivian artist's US court case on copyright.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Supported the bill, thanking the sponsor and the President, and asked that it be strengthened at committee stage.
Said four education bills are planned in the legislative agenda and invited the MDP to join the debate.
Criticised the MDP for raising urgent questions and then not staying for the debate.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported updating the law and asked that experts be invited to the committee stage.
Noted the amendments extend the protection term from 50 to 70 years.
Said earlier Majlis bills were poorly implemented, and urged supporting the government's work.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill and said the previous government left creators' rights unprotected.
Criticised the MDP walk-out during the debate.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Raised a point of order that the member was straying from the bill under debate.
Called the bill very important, noting only one amendment in about 13 years.
Criticised the MDP for raising urgent questions that take up Majlis time.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill; said the sponsor and the government deserve thanks.
Said many Maldivian artisans and creators suffer from copying and that the amendments address this.
Rejected MDP claims about the economy and allowances.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Introduced the bill on behalf of the government: amendments to better protect the rights of artists and creators.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Supported the amendment and cited copyright cases abroad as reasons creators' rights need protecting.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the bill; said creative works should be marketable abroad and self-employment should be encouraged.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill and asked that it go to committee so it can be implemented quickly.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, including the protection period, and criticised the use of urgent motions.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill; said young creators have gone unpaid and brand imports can harm Maldivians.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Thanked the sponsor; criticised the MDP's urgent motion and the government's spending on student transfers.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Supported the bill and linked it to Islamic teaching on respecting others' work.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Supported the bill and the 70-year protection period; called for a regulating body.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the bill and gave a view on one amendment on compensation for infringement, asking committee to study it further.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill; said the stakes for young creators outweigh the urgent motion.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Supported the bill and spoke of constitutional rights, including utilities in the islands.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill and proposed protection for the whole lifetime of the creator rather than 70 years.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Supported the bill and said urgent motions waste the Majlis's time.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Backed the bill as protecting small and mid-sized Maldivian businesses and artists' brands and products.
Said the MDP's urgent questions are raised to disrupt the day's business.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill as important legal protection for artists and creators.
Criticised the MDP's urgent question and the MDP's absence from the floor, saying halted work costs the public.
Cited counterfeit household goods causing health problems as a reason for the bill.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to repeated statements that no MDP member was on the floor, noting some were in committee.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Raised a point of order saying his urgent question was about students from his constituency not receiving allowances, not about wasting time.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Said the amendments would benefit the film, music and other creative industries.
Said the MDP's claims that students abroad were not being paid were untrue, citing ministry payments.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shifaz
positions: Supported the amendments as important for rights and progress of Maldivian creators and thanked the sponsor and the President.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the bill but said laws and court judgments matter only if governments enforce them.
Criticised daily MDP urgent questions as wasting the chamber's time.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill as protecting artists' rights, saying the government sent it to the Majlis.
Said the MDP's urgent questions lacked substance and that overseas students are being paid.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Said the main complaint of creators is weak enforcement of the 2010 law, citing consultations with artists.
Noted a ministry copyright counter reportedly stopped working after 2019 and raised concern about registration fees.

speakers.name: Azim Abdul Azeez
positions: Supported the amendments to protect artists and workers' rights and thanked the sponsor and the President.
Called for limits on how urgent questions can be submitted, and for the bill to go to committee.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the amendments are important but noted penalties rose only in fine amounts and enforcement is the real weakness.
Proposed sending the bill to committee to strengthen enforcement powers.
Defended the MDP's right to raise urgent questions as a minority party.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 5 to 8 were accepted without amendment.
Committee membership changes were announced by the chair.
The urgent matter on payments to students abroad did not get enough votes to be debated.
A 30-minute break was taken from 10:31 to 11:01.
The Speaker accepted a point of order from Kanditheemu but asked members to speak accurately about attendance.
Points of order from North Galolhu and South Hithadhoo were not accepted by the chair.
A recess ran from 12:34 to 13:06 before debate resumed under the Deputy Speaker.
No vote was taken on the Copyright bill; the sitting was closed so committees could meet.
Next sitting set for Tuesday 9 July 2024 at 09:00.

votes.what: Whether to debate the urgent matter on payments to students studying abroad (needed 36 of 71 voting)
Whether to take up for debate the urgent question submitted by MP Ibrahim Nazil (open vote, 9:14 AM; 72 present, 71 eligible)
